name: Standard Rock Route
overview: Pernod is the highest of the four Wine Spires (Burgundy, Chianti, Chablis, and Pernod) above Washington Pass. Fred Beckey, Dick McGowan, and Don Wilde made the first ascent in September 1952, an aid-heavy climb by today's standards: pitons for both protection and direct aid, a hand-drilled Rawl-drive bolt to protect an insecure section, another bolt to facilitate an 8-foot pendulum around an overhanging, holdless corner, and more bolts placed from a shoulder-stand to reach the summit. The modern route follows essentially the same line, reached via the long Burgundy Col approach.
beta: Pernod and neighboring Chablis are the easiest of the Wine Spires, and this line is a reasonable day from a Burgundy Col camp. The climbing is moderate (about 5.5-5.7) and not sustained. It climbs from the east side up to the notch between Pernod and Chianti and then up the northeast corner to a tiny summit block; the South Face and the Direct West Face are separate, harder routes on the same spire.
descent_text: This is a rappel descent, not a walk-off. Rappel from the summit block back to the notch between Pernod and Chianti, then make long rappels down the east side to the snow and névé at the edge of the Silver Star Glacier basin. No rappel count is published for this line; carry double ropes, and cord to back up or replace old slings and bolts. From the glacier edge, traverse back north below Chianti and climb a few hundred feet to regain Burgundy Col, then descend the climbers' trail (scree, the bench, then the timbered rib) to the SR-20 pullout. Watch for moats along the rock late in the season, and budget real time for the loose scree below the col.
descent: Descend via the standard descent route, retracing the ascent when possible. Be aware of loose rock and snow bridge hazards. Maintain group cohesion on exposed sections.
rappels: Several: from the summit back to the Pernod–Chianti notch, then long rappels down the east side to the glacier edge (no published count)
rappel_count_note: No published count: rappels lead from the summit back to the notch between Pernod and Chianti, then long rappels on double ropes descend the east side to the glacier edge.

pitch_detail.notes: From below the east walls, climb obliquely up and around to the notch between Pernod and Chianti; roughly three pitches, mostly 4th and 5th class.
pitch_detail.pitch: East side to the Pernod–Chianti notch

pitch_detail.notes: From the notch the line goes up the northeast corner. The first-ascent party used aid, a bolt to protect an insecure section and a bolt for an 8-foot pendulum around an overhanging corner, and reached the small summit block with bolts placed from a shoulder stand; the old fixed bolts are worth inspecting and backing up.

fa: First ascent 1952 — Don Wilde, Dick McGowan, and Fred Beckey.
